newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-TARANGO "GUARANTEED" NOT TO RUN INTO REBEUH AGAIN.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-TARANGO "GUARANTEED" NOT TO RUN INTO REBEUH AGAIN.

text.p: American Jeff Tarango said on Thursday he had received a guarantee the referee at the centre of his 1995 Wimbledon walkout would never officiate at one of his matches again.
Tarango, banned from last year's Wimbledon tournament, plans another visit to the All England Club this year -- but this time will not run into French chair umpire Bruno Rebeuh.
"I've been given that guarantee, yes," he said, without naming the official who made the assurance. "Anytime I mention a name I get into trouble."
Tarango was originally banned for two Grand Slam events and fined US$43,756 for storming off the court during his third round clash at Wimbledon.
Before leaving the court he accused Rebeuh of being "the most corrupt official in the game" and later charged him with favouring certain players.
His wife shared the newspaper headlines for slapping the umpire in the face.
But Tarango made a public apology, earning a reprieve from the game's establishment, which reduced the fine to $28,256 and a ban from one Grand Slam event -- last year's Wimbledon.
Tarango, ranked 93 in the world, said there were no hard feelings between himself and organisers of the Wimbledon tournament.
"It's not anything personal at all as far as me and Wimbledon are concerned," he said after a 6-4 6-1 6-1 second round victory over Switzerland's Marc Rosset at the Australian Open on Thursday.
"I don't hold any animosity towards Wimbledon, I think it is the greatest tournament on earth.
"It has a lot of prestige and hopefully I can go there and kick some ass."
Tarango said his 'bad-boy' image had frightened off potential sponsors and he now wears all-white clothing handmade by his mother.
"I think the all-white is just fine for this year," he said, referring to Wimbledon's strict dress code which dictates players wear predominantly white.
The left-hander, who lives in France, admits his personality undergoes a metamorphis when he takes the court.
"When I'm on court I'm intense, I'm fired up, I'm going to massacre anyone that's on the other side of the net," Tarango said.
"My dad has never been able to explain it. I tell him it's his fault for being a boxer and getting hit in the head too much."
Tarango will face 11th seed Jim Courier in the third round of the Australian Open.
